note: COBOL intrinsic FUNCTIONs that gnucobol-rs's front-end does NOT wire because they fall outside the oracle-first byte-identity subset. gnucobol-rs wires 77/110 intrinsics, each proven byte-identical to the admitted GnuCOBOL 3.2 cobc; these 33 are the boundary. Recorded as a build plan for a SEPARATE kobold-side layer that may implement them with its own conformance model (not the GnuCOBOL 3.2 byte oracle). DATA ONLY: no gnucobol/libcob GPL source is included. Companion to frontend-boundary-verbs-build-plan.json.
source: gnucobol-rs COBOL-PARITY.md intrinsic census -- 77/110 wired + proven byte-identical, 33 boundary (these).
boundary: gnucobol-rs's bar is byte-identity with GnuCOBOL 3.2 cobc. These 33 have no fixed cobc output to match -- libcob leaves some unimplemented, others return live program/host/locale state or non-deterministic values, and a few are libcob-internal helpers cobc rejects as user functions. Implementing them is therefore a non-oracle effort that belongs OUTSIDE the faithful port.

functions.why_boundary_in_gnucobol_rs: libcob itself does not implement it in GnuCOBOL 3.2 -- the ported cob_intr_* is an error_not_implemented stub mirroring the oracle, so there is no runtime behaviour to reproduce
functions.build_intent: port the libcob runtime semantics first (a RUNTIME gap, not a front-end gap); once the cob_intr_* is real the front-end wires for free
